chapter: New Orleans, Havana and back to New York
title: Band shorts for Will Cowan and Snader Telescriptions
summary: They sort out the film shorts he made for Cowan at Universal and for Snader, shown originally in bar machines, and the union's confusion over them.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Including the Snader -- the things that became Snader Telescriptions, which were something else when they were made, right? The shorts that were made out at Universal?
Oh yeah.
They were made by Les Cowan, was that his name?
Oh, Will Cowan.
Oh, Will Cowan. Yeah.
That's his boat right there, the Alma Lee.
Oh.
And we see each other all the time.
Those were some great band shorts. He sold them to Snader, right?
No, Snader made their own.
Oh. Well, I say that because Duke made two for Cowan at Universal, which was in '49 and '50, and
they later showed up on Snader Telescriptions.

Well, they must have made some kind of a deal with Universal. But I remember I made one for him, or maybe two, I don't know. But we didn't do them at Universal. We did them at some other studio, and I remember the musicians' union was there, they couldn't figure out what was going on and they were very upset. They didn't know how to classify this type of endeavor. And they were watching the whole thing very closely. But that definitely was not made -- that was made directly for him.
For Snader.
Yeah.
Oh. Well it must have been later. Do you know what year that was?
Oh, that was in the -- oh, that's got to be in the late '40s.
Yeah. Yeah, that would fit. Late '40s or --
Because they were made for -- were they made for television or for these boxes in the bars?
Well, the firm was at least later known as Snader Telescriptions, so --
It seems to me they were originally made to be shown in bars.
Yeah, I think so too, in those little
machines.

Yes. So that could have been earlier, although I recall distinctly that Gene Roland Rowland was playing trumpet in the band that we made these things for, and I didn't know Gene, Gene never worked for me until late in -- the late '40s. So it's -- but now with Will Cowan, those were all done at Universal, and it was an entirely different thing.

Well, at one point, after we've gone through the chronological thing I want to go through and read off -- because these are not, unfortunately, chronological. These are alphabetical in order, and so we'll go through and --
Well, I wouldn't know the names of the shorts.
But you might remember them by date or something, or by circumstance.
I made quite a few for Will, I think.
Well, we'll check that.
Yeah, okay.
Later on. It's interesting, though. I mean there's this long list of references, after your name,
Yeah.
